reasons: The cited § (h) grants Customer (AP) the affiliate / asset-purchaser / merger-successor carve-out required by the preferred position and subjects all other assignments to consent that 'shall not be unreasonably withheld', so it meets at least the fallback ('mutual right to assign to successors; consent not unreasonably withheld') on its material terms.

No walk-away trigger is present: there is no blanket bar on Customer assignment and no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right for Kubient anywhere in the cited text or termination provisions.

The two shortfalls noted (no express bar on Vendor assigning to a Customer competitor; symmetric rather than one-way consent relief) are minor sub-elements short of preferred wording and are correctly recorded in the rationale rather than redlined.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was rendered (redline text is identical to the original) and no counterparty comment was proposed; the deterministic check confirming the successor/affiliate carve-out supports the classification.

The rationale's treatment of the § 2 'non-transferable, non-assignable' licence-scope language as a grant limitation rather than an assignment restriction is a reasonable reading and does not undermine the compliant call.
